name: Sandy Lane
positioning: Neo-Palladian beach resort in Barbados on a former sugar plantation, with rooms, suites, penthouses and a private five-bedroom villa
best_for: Families wanting a children's club, a teen den and holiday sports camps
Travelers who want beachfront rooms with direct access to the sand
Groups wanting a private villa with its own butler and chef

facts.text: Sandy Lane's accommodations are in a Neo-Palladian style.
The resort stands on the site of a onetime sugar plantation.
Accommodation ranges from guest rooms and suites to penthouses and a five-bedroom villa.
The Sandy Lane Suite comes with personalised butler service.
The Villa at Sandy Lane is hidden behind private gates within manicured gardens.
Suites in the Dolphin and Orchid wings feature Italian marble floors and plantation-style heirloom furniture.
The Luxury Orchid Suites have private verandas set within private gardens.
The two-bedroom Luxury Dolphin Suites are aimed at families and have private terraces with sea views.
During school holidays, children can join sports camps in swimming, water-skiing, golf, tennis and football.
L'Acajou is an open-air restaurant serving French and Mediterranean specialties.

highlights.text: The Ocean Rooms are beachfront rooms so close to the sea that guests can step out of the room and stroll to the water and sand.
The five-bedroom Villa at Sandy Lane comes with its own Villa Butler and Villa Chef.
The Sandy Lane Suite offers sunset views from a terrace infinity pool and direct access to Sandy Lane's stretch of white sand beach.
The Treehouse Club for children runs activities such as sailing, outdoor movie nights and themed dinner parties.
Teenagers have their own Den with pool tables, table football, a jukebox and a mocktail bar.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing that reflects the resort's premium positioning.
WhataHotel notes that formal dress codes apply in certain areas and restaurants.
